title: Neighborhood Stability
statement: In every finite simple triangle-free graph G and every vertex v, the open neighborhood N(v) is a stable set.
proof_route: If two vertices of N(v) were adjacent, they and v would form a triangle.

title: Union-of-Neighborhoods Coloring Bound
statement: For every finite S subset V(G) in a triangle-free graph, χ(G[⋃_{s∈S} N(s)]) ≤ |S|.
proof_route: Order S. Assign each vertex in the union to its first neighboring s. Each color class lies inside one stable neighborhood N(s).

title: Isolate-Sharp Closed-Neighborhood Bound
statement: Let I be the set of vertices isolated in G[S]. Then χ(G[N[S]]) ≤ |S| if I is empty, and χ(G[N[S]]) ≤ |S|+1 otherwise.
proof_route: Every non-isolated vertex of S already lies in ⋃_{s∈S}N(s). Color that union with |S| colors by N02. The isolated vertices I form a stable set and require at most one additional color.
novelty_query: triangle-free closed neighborhood chromatic bound isolated vertices

title: Connected Closed-Neighborhood Bound
statement: If G is triangle-free and G[S] is connected with |S|≥2, then χ(G[N[S]]) ≤ |S|.
proof_route: A connected graph with at least two vertices has no isolated vertices; apply N03.

title: Protected Chromatic Remainder Bound
statement: If G is triangle-free and G[S] has no isolated vertices, then χ(G-N[S]) ≥ χ(G)-|S|.
proof_route: Color G[N[S]] using at most |S| colors by N03 and color the remainder separately. Since χ(G) is at most the sum, rearrange.
novelty_query: triangle-free chromatic number after deleting closed neighborhood connected set

title: Finite-Set Survival in Infinite Chromatic Graphs
statement: If G is triangle-free with infinite chromatic number and S is finite with G[S] having no isolated vertices, then G-N[S] still has infinite chromatic number.
proof_route: Otherwise G[N[S]] and G-N[S] would both have finite chromatic number; N03 gives the first, contradicting χ(G)=∞.
novelty_query: Finite-Set Survival in Infinite Chromatic Graphs

title: Sequential Protected Deletion Ledger
statement: Let G0=G. For i=1,…,m, let S_i⊆V(G_{i-1}) induce no isolated vertices in G_{i-1}, and put G_i=G_{i-1}-N_{G_{i-1}}[S_i]. Then χ(G_m) ≥ χ(G)-Σ_i |S_i|.
proof_route: Apply N05 inside each current graph and telescope the inequalities.
novelty_query: sequential closed neighborhood deletion chromatic budget triangle-free

title: Edge Closed-Neighborhood Bipartiteness
statement: If uv is an edge of a triangle-free graph, then G[N[{u,v}]] is bipartite with parts N(u) and N(v), and therefore has chromatic number at most 2.
proof_route: N(u) and N(v) are stable. They are disjoint because a common neighbor would make a triangle; u∈N(v) and v∈N(u), so their union is exactly the closed neighborhood of {u,v}.

title: Common-Neighborhood Stability
statement: For any two vertices u,v in a triangle-free graph, N(u)∩N(v) is stable.
proof_route: An edge inside the common neighborhood together with u would form a triangle.

title: Induced Two-Pole Fan
statement: If u and v are nonadjacent in a triangle-free graph and |N(u)∩N(v)|≥m, then G contains an induced K_{2,m} with poles u,v.
proof_route: Choose m common neighbors. They are stable by N09, the poles are nonadjacent, and all pole-to-leaf edges are present.

title: One-Sided Attachment to an Induced Biclique
statement: If (A,B) induces a nonempty complete bipartite graph in a triangle-free graph and x∉A∪B, then x has neighbors in at most one of A and B.
proof_route: A neighbor a∈A and b∈B would satisfy ab∈E and create triangle xab.
novelty_query: One-Sided Attachment to an Induced Biclique

title: Connected Dominator Chromatic Bound
statement: If S is a connected dominating vertex set with |S|≥2 in a triangle-free graph G, then χ(G)≤|S|.

title: Quantitative Critical Escape Component
statement: Let G be a finite k-vertex-critical triangle-free graph. If H=G[S] is connected, 2≤|S|<k, then some component C of G-N[S] satisfies χ(C)≥k-|S|.
proof_route: N05 gives χ(G-N[S])≥k-|S|. The chromatic number of a disjoint union is the maximum over components.
novelty_query: critical triangle-free graph component outside closed neighborhood chromatic number
